generation_inputs.preparation: Exact 32x nearest-neighbour enlargement of native 24x24 PNG, without recolouring or aspect correction.

prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: NEW continuous high-resolution illustrated water texture for a strategy game remake, full opaque square.
Reference image: original Amiga all-water tile. Treat its jagged pixels as coarse samples of a continuous water surface, NOT as shapes to preserve. Reconstruct the flowing natural water that could have produced the image. Keep overall muted teal #448899 water, darker #335566 troughs, occasional #55bbbb turquoise reflection ridges and very sparse light-grey/white glints. Preserve the approximate broad diagonal sweep of wave bands from lower left toward upper right, their coarse spacing, lighting balance and approximate placement of the strongest glints. Aim for very similar appearance when bilinear-reduced to24x24.
At high resolution redraw every wave as a continuous curved ridge with tapered irregular foam, connected water flow and smooth organic transitions. Turn isolated bright pixel squares into tiny curved reflections embedded in the wave crests. Replace all stepped block boundaries with natural curved water contours. Show one coherent water surface with delicate smaller ripples and clear continuous fine detail. NO square cells with wave textures inside; no grid, rectangular colour patches, staircase boundaries, blocky bands, checkerboard, pixel art, voxels or filtered enlarged pixels. Avoid uniformly repeated bright strokes. Diffuse lighting, overhead orthographic game-material illustration. No shore, ground, rocks, vegetation, boats, bridge, horizon, border, text, hex outline or shadows from unseen objects. Fill the entire opaque square including corners with water. Goal: continuous natural high-resolution painted water, retaining original broad composition and colour balance without tracing pixel topology.
cleanup: Source retained unchanged. Lanczos3 reduction source→unmasked96; independent unmasked96→48 and96→24. Apply original diagnostic footprint independently after filtering. No source painting, recoloring or alpha repair. Preserve original stepped mask only as reference coverage; continuous production contours remain separate geometry work.
review: User accepts continuous style for all terrain. Current exports/reviews use fixed Lanczos3; historical bilinear outputs retained. Approximately90% native visual resemblance and shared-edge acceptance remain open; style approval is not a numeric score. See docs/art/terrain-production.md and docs/art/native-material-pilot.md.
determinism: AI reruns are not assumed deterministic; exports reproduce locally from retained source using tools/art-review.

resampling.algorithm: Separable antialiased Lanczos3, kernel sinc(t)*sinc(t/3), radius 3 widened by source/destination per axis; pixel centers (d+0.5)*source/destination-0.5. Clip support to image and renormalize. Integer-coordinate distances, Go math.Sin kernel, row-major float64 sums without intermediate quantization; premultiplied byte RGB (no linear-light conversion). For positive raw alpha, clamp premultiplied channels to [0,255*raw alpha] before unpremultiplying; independently clamp alpha to [0,255], preserving constant straight color through alpha overshoot. Round half up once per reduction; zero RGB at zero output alpha.
chain: raw4x/raw2x/rawNative -> outputs: apply reference footprint independently

historical_bilinear_resampling.algorithm: Separable antialiased tent, radius source/destination per axis; pixel centers (d+0.5)*source/destination-0.5. Clip support to image and renormalize. Integer-coordinate weights, row-major float64 sums; alpha-weighted byte RGB (no linear-light conversion), unpremultiply and round half up once per reduction; zero RGB at zero output alpha.
chain: raw4x/raw2x/rawNative -> outputs: apply reference footprint independently

style_approval.scope: User approves continuous revision-02 direction for all terrain tiles; subsequent filter choice is Lanczos.
style_approval.limitations: Per-asset approximately90% native visual resemblance, shared edges and runtime pack acceptance are still reviewed separately.
